Phonosemantic compound. 欠 represents the meaning and 哥 represents the sound.
詠也。从欠哥聲。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *kaːl): phonetic 哥 (OC *kaːl) + semantic 欠 (“blow”). Specialized form of 哥 (OC *kaːl, “to sing”).
From Proto-Sino-Tibetan *gaːr ~ *ga (“to dance; to sing; to leap; to stride”). Cognate with Burmese က (ka., “to dance”).

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, received 欠部 text
evidence.text: The entry defines 歌 as “詠也” and analyzes it as 从欠哥聲. The same section describes 欠 as a person with an open mouth and breath rising out. This supports 欠 as the semantic classifier and 哥 as the phonetic component in the received seal-script-era analysis; it does not by itself verify the character’s earliest form.
evidence.title: 說文解字/08 - 維基文庫

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: Records the Shuowen explanation “詠也。从欠，哥聲” and a variant 謌 “或从言.” It cites 《詩經·魏風·園有桃》 “心之憂矣，我歌且謠” for the verbal sense singing; it separately records praise, melodic song, and a singable poetic genre. The page does not date the poem’s composition, so this supplies an early textual citation but not a secure date for the extant written graph.
evidence.title: 歌 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: This compilation reports a bronze form in the Yu Fei Er Zhong (余贎兒鐘), catalogued as 集成184 and dated late Spring and Autumn, with structure 言+可; it also lists a Warring States form, Chu manuscript evidence, Shuowen forms, and a Qin Shuihudi slip form. Its prose says later forms are 欠+哥 and notes an alternate 言+哥 form. The chronology is a secondary collation, and its analysis that 哥 contributes meaning as well as sound is not established by the Shuowen phonetic notation.
evidence.title: 歌字形演变字源_汉字「歌」

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, 可部 entry 哥, online text with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The entry states “哥，聲也。从二可。古文以爲謌字.” Duan Yucai’s note says the sense “sound” is not attested in use in his time and that Han texts often used 哥 for 歌. This supports an old graphic association of 哥 with 謌/歌, but does not establish that standalone 哥 originally meant “to sing,” or that its graphic form developed chronologically from another form.
evidence.title: 說文解字「哥」

evidence.source: Wiktionary, Chinese character entry 歌; reconstruction data attributed to Baxter–Sagart (2014) and Zhengzhang (2003)
evidence.text: Lists 哥 and 歌 together at Zhengzhang Old Chinese *kaːl; for 歌 it gives Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[k]ˤaj and Middle Chinese ka, with modern Mandarin gē. This supports a historical sound relationship between the written phonetic and compound character under those reconstruction systems. These are reconstructions, not direct recordings, and this entry does not give 哥’s Baxter–Sagart form on this page.
evidence.title: 歌 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary, character-page Mandarin and Cantonese readings
evidence.text: Gives standard Mandarin gē (Pinyin) and Guangzhou/Hong Kong Cantonese go1 (Jyutping) for 歌. These are readings of the character/word, not evidence of the character’s formation.
evidence.title: 歌 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary, character-page Old Chinese phonology table
evidence.text: For 歌, the page lists Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese *kaːl and Baxter–Sagart (2014) *[k]ˤaj. In its Zhengzhang phonetic-series table it lists 哥 *kaːl. Both characters therefore align in the same Zhengzhang reconstruction system; the page does not provide equivalent Baxter–Sagart data for 哥 here, so do not compare the *kaːl form directly with 歌’s Baxter–Sagart form.
evidence.title: 歌 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Kangxi Dictionary text as reproduced by 汉典
evidence.text: The entry cites 《詩經·魏風》 “我歌且謠,” 《書·舜典》 “詩言志，歌永言,” and 《禮記·樂記》 on singing as lengthened utterance. It distinguishes musical song from unaccompanied 謠 in the commentary to 《園有桃》 and records a further use of 歌鐘 in 《左傳·襄公十一年》. It also preserves later senses such as praising and a bell name. These citations show textual uses and later semantic range, but their order in a dictionary list is not a chronology of semantic change.
evidence.title: 歌 gē - 汉典

evidence.text: The 2014 book describes its work as a reconstruction of Old Chinese phonology, morphology, and lexicon, the language of the earliest Chinese classical texts and ancestor of later Chinese varieties. This contextualizes the reconstructions as scholarly models rather than directly attested pronunciations.
evidence.title: Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction

evidence.text: The page proposes Proto-Sino-Tibetan *gaːr ~ *ga ‘dance; sing; leap; stride’ and compares Burmese က ka ‘dance.’ This is a separate lexical etymology claim, not evidence for the graphic formation of 歌. The inspected page gives no early dated Burmese attestation or independently inspected comparative source, so the cognacy and semantic pathway remain provisional here.

gaps: No visually inspected inscription image was available in this research, so the reported bronze and manuscript glyph readings were not independently checked from the artifacts or facsimiles.

The inscription compilation reports a Spring and Autumn bronze form with 言+可 and later 欠+哥 forms, but the transition and component-by-component lineage are not proven by the opened sources. Do not assign a definite earlier_form or full_form relation to components solely from these different reported shapes; use uncertain when a distinct origin_form requires classification.

Shuowen directly supports 欠 as the semantic classifier and 哥 as sound in its analyzed form. Whether the early 言+可 bronze graph is an earlier form of the later 欠+哥 graph, a graphic variant, or a related spelling needs specialist paleographic corroboration.

The standalone 哥 component has Mandarin gē and is grouped with 歌 at Zhengzhang *kaːl in the inspected comparison table. Equivalent same-system Baxter–Sagart data for 哥 was not established in the inspected page; avoid implying the two reconstructions are identical across systems.

The poem 《園有桃》 is cited by dictionaries for early use of 歌 as singing, but the reviewed sources did not establish the poem’s composition date or the date of a physical manuscript bearing the graph. Earliest secure graph attestation and earliest word use remain unresolved.
Later senses (praise, musical piece, verse genre, bell name) are attested in cited classical texts, but no source consulted established when or by what semantic steps these senses developed.

The proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison with Burmese ka ‘dance’ was not independently verified through a primary comparative source or early Burmese attestations; keep it separate from character graphic history and label it uncertain.
No evidence supports a graph-loan analysis for 歌 in this research. The Shuowen note that 哥 could write 謌/歌 is relevant to graph usage, but is not proof that 歌 itself originated as a whole-graph loan.
The late Spring-and-Autumn bronze and Warring States forms are reported by a secondary collation; their artifact images and readings were not independently checked against primary facsimiles.
